observations: Files I read: the request JSON (with its first reading), source/original.txt and REVISION-2026-11-11.md. I opened these images with Read and looked at them myself, in this order: workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-04.png, then workflow/storyboards/page-04.png, then workflow/review/page-03.png, review/page-04.png and review/page-05.png. I did not render the SVGs, and I did not open the character sheets.

The script matches the source: 'Soon, his slot comes up.' / 'NOW · A-12'; 'A quick vitals check first.' / Nurse 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.' (the r13 line, which no longer repeats the caption); 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.' / 'RAVI · READY'.

Typography note, not blocking: in both the storyboard and review/page-04.png, 'RAVI · READY' wraps after the middle dot, so the dot ends the first line. Both words stay on the same tablet card, read top to bottom, and the meaning does not change. This is a minor lettering-stage tidy-up, not a reading-order problem.

Unnumbered page-04.png: in the top tier the caption (top left) comes before the label (top right). In the bottom-left tier the caption (top left) comes before the nurse's balloon (mid right), whose short tail points down to the nurse. In the bottom-right tier the caption at top comes before the RAVI · READY label low on the page. The intended order is the only natural one.

First-reader point: Ravi gives no reply to the nurse. In review/page-04.png he is seated, smiling and relaxed with his forearm resting on the table and the cuff on, so his acting carries his response, and the nurse's line is an instruction that needs no spoken answer. Acceptable.
First-reader point: the nurse is unintroduced. The caption 'A quick vitals check first.', her lavender scrubs and lanyard, and the BP bulb in her hand establish her role at once. Acceptable.
First-reader point: Meera's role in Panel A. She sits at the reception monitor in the background, which keeps the reception setting continuous. She does not need to act. Acceptable.

First-reader point: the large empty lower areas in Panels B and C are placeholder artefacts. In the art, the full figures with the vitals kit fill Panel B, and Ananya with the tablet fills Panel C, with the label on the tablet screen. 'his', in 'his slot', relies on page 03, which immediately precedes it.
